# Vadim Sokolov

> The website of Vadim Sokolov: research, teaching and books. The books are free to read, and each one has a page with its description and how to cite it. A book with results also has a page with its results and their numbers.

Each book has a Markdown page with its description and how to cite it. A book with results also has its main results on that page and a Markdown page with all its results by chapter with their numbers. A summary of each chapter is linked under the book. The full text is the PDF and the source on GitHub, under CC BY 4.0. To prove, check or extend a result of a book that has results, start with the catalog that is linked under that book: it lists every result with its status, including the open and conditional ones. When you use a result, cite the book and the number of the result.

## Bayesian Clinical Trials

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 12 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or computed), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the Quarto file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.2.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayesian Clinical Trials](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/index.html.md): by Alexandra Sokolova, Vadim Sokolov and Nicholas G. Polson (2026). Bayesian clinical trials built up from the traditional trial and tied to regulation: calibration, monitoring, safety, borrowing, adaptive designs, and reanalyses of landmark trials, with an R package and an online lab. Keywords: Bayesian clinical trials, adaptive trial design, group sequential design, interim monitoring, type I error calibration, FDA Bayesian guidance, multiplicity and shrinkage, informative priors, e-values, operating characteristics simulation, biostatistics, R package.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24147174): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24147174 for version 1.2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24122875 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html.md): 12 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/RESULTS.md): 12 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/releases/download/v1.2.0/bayesian_clinical_trials.pdf): 612 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/tree/v1.2.0): the Quarto source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [The book as a website](https://vsokolov.org/bayesian_clinical_trials/): every chapter as a page, with search
- [Main result: The three deviation scales (evidence tolls)](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#evidence_tolls_three_scales): Section 11.9.2, page 253, proved. A fixed level test, a Bayes rule and an anytime valid rule act at three different sizes of the squared standardized score; for the normal mixture the anytime valid bar exceeds the Bayes bar by a surcharge that is about 2 log(1/alpha) at large information.
- [Main result: The surcharge for validity at every stopping time is about 70 per cent of the fixed trial requirement, as a comparison of boundary terms](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#surcharge_seventy_percent): Section 11.9.4, page 256, proved. For the normal mixture e value rule, against the uncalibrated Bayes factor bar (posterior odds of one), the large information surcharge 7.38 is about 70 per cent of the fixed trial standardized requirement 10.51; this compares boundary terms and is not an exact sample size identity.
- [Main result: Moderate deviation sample size equation](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#moderate_deviation_sample_size): Section 9.3.2, page 202, proved. A Bayes rule whose bar grows like the logarithm of the sample size has an implicit sample size equation, the textbook formula with the critical value replaced by the square root of log n plus a constant.
- [Main result: Calibration of a posterior probability rule by the null maximum](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#null_maximum_calibration): Section 14.4.1, page 309, proved. The smallest threshold that holds a monitored posterior probability rule to level alpha is the (1 minus alpha) quantile of the largest posterior probability reached over the looks in null simulations, so one simulation serves every threshold.
- [Main result: Exact backward induction for binary endpoints on a cubic lattice](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#backward_induction_states): Section 15.6.2, page 342, proved. For a two arm binary trial the Bayes optimal stopping rule depends only on the success counts and the stage, so backward induction is exact on a lattice of order T cubed states.
- [Main result: SELECT reconstruction, median events at decision with conditioning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#select_reconstruction_medians): Section 21.1.2, page 476, computed. In our reconstruction of SELECT at hazard ratio 0.80, a calibrated Bayesian rule stops at a median of 464 events among trials that declare efficacy and 486 over all trials, against 817 for SELECT's planned design (one interim analysis with Lan-DeMets spending, then the final); the e value rule and a four look design are slower or less powerful.
- [Main result: Reproduction of the BNT162b2 beta binomial analysis](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#bnt162b2_beta_binomial_reproduction): Section 6.12.1, page 136, computed. The statistical analysis plan's beta binomial model with a Beta(0.700102, 1) prior, applied to 8 versus 162 cases, gives a posterior probability that vaccine efficacy exceeds 30 per cent of 1 minus 2e-28 and a point estimate of 95 per cent, matching the published interval within a tenth of a point.
- [Computed: Reproduction of the BNT162b2 beta binomial analysis](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#bnt162b2_beta_binomial_reproduction): Section 6.12.1, page 136
- [Computed: The Bayes factor bar exceeds the fixed level bar once information times prior variance passes about 46](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#bayes_bar_crossing_46): Section 7.5.1, page 148
- [Computed: Moderate deviation and textbook sizes at the SELECT hazard ratio of 0.80 (not a prediction of SELECT's size)](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#moderate_deviation_select_comparison): Section 9.3.6, page 207
- [Computed: Four operation ulcer example, adjusted p value against posterior probability](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#ulcer_bonferroni_vs_posterior): Section 10.5.3, page 232
- [Computed: A utility only backward induction rule declares treatment better half the time under the null](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#utility_only_rule_null_declaration): Section 15.6.3, page 345
- [Computed: Shared control false positive counts for four arms](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#shared_control_false_positive_counts): Section 20.4.1, page 452
- [Computed: SELECT reconstruction, median events at decision with conditioning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#select_reconstruction_medians): Section 21.1.2, page 476
- [Chapter 1. A Trial Is a Decision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/01_a_trial_is_a_decision.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 2. The Life of a Drug: Phases I to IV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/02_the_life_of_a_drug_phases_i_to_iv.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 3. The Regulatory Framework](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/03_the_regulatory_framework.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 4. Are They Different? Testing From the Ground Up](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/04_are_they_different_testing_from_the_ground_up.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 5. Randomization From the Ground Up](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/05_randomization_from_the_ground_up.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 6. Prior, Likelihood, Posterior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/06_prior_likelihood_posterior.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 7. Weighing Evidence: p-values, Bayes Factors, and Posterior Probabilities](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/07_weighing_evidence_p_values_bayes_factors_and_posterior.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 8. Choosing and Defending Priors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/08_choosing_and_defending_priors.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 9. Error Rates, Power, and Sample Size](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/09_error_rates_power_and_sample_size.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 10. Multiplicity and Shrinkage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/10_multiplicity_and_shrinkage.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 11. Interim Looks and the Three Deviation Scales](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/11_interim_looks_and_the_three_deviation_scales.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 12. Anytime-Valid Inference and E-values](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/12_anytime_valid_inference_and_e_values.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 13. Safety Signals and Safety Monitoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/summaries/13_safety_signals_and_safety_monitoring.md): summary of the chapter and its results

## Bayesian Clinical Trials and Personalized Medicine: Volume I: Bayesian Clinical Trials

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 12 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or computed), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the Quarto file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.1.3 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayesian Clinical Trials and Personalized Medicine: Volume I: Bayesian Clinical Trials](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/index.html.md): by Alexandra Sokolova, Vadim Sokolov and Nicholas G. Polson (2026). Volume I of a two volume series. Bayesian clinical trials built up from the traditional trial and tied to regulation: calibration, monitoring, safety, borrowing, adaptive designs, and reanalyses of landmark trials, with an R package and an online lab. Keywords: Bayesian clinical trials, adaptive trial design, group sequential design, interim monitoring, type I error calibration, FDA Bayesian guidance, multiplicity and shrinkage, informative priors, e-values, operating characteristics simulation, biostatistics, R package.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24141732): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24141732 for version 1.1.3 (10.5281/zenodo.24122875 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page

## Bayes and Law: Evidence, Expected Utility and Machines in the Courtroom

- [Bayes and Law: Evidence, Expected Utility and Machines in the Courtroom](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_law/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). A casebook for law students on reasoning under uncertainty: priors, likelihood ratios, standards of proof as decision thresholds, the classic fallacies, and the statistics, economics and machines that now enter the courtroom, taught through leading English, American and comparative cases. Keywords: Bayesian reasoning in law, likelihood ratio, weight of evidence, standards of proof, decision theory, expected utility, forensic statistics, prosecutor's fallacy, statistics as evidence, law and economics, artificial intelligence and law, algorithmic fairness.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24138404): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24138404 for version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24138403 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page

## On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 132 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, computed, conditional or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.4.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Why the Collatz (3x+1) conjecture resists proof: the map as a random walk, an optimizer and a Diophantine problem; proofs that fixed horizon monotone Lyapunov certificates and finite residue sieves cannot settle it and the cycle inequality cannot exclude all cycles; a momentum method from log2 3. Keywords: Collatz conjecture, 3x+1 problem, Syracuse map, parity vectors, Lyapunov functions, majorization minimization, Nesterov momentum, martingales, continued fractions, Collatz cycles, Diophantine approximation, first order optimization methods.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24113412): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24113412 for version 1.4.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23331099 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html.md): 132 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/main/RESULTS.md): 132 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/releases/download/v1.4.0/collatz.pdf): 445 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/tree/v1.4.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: No fixed horizon monotone certificate for Collatz descent](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#no_fixed_horizon_monotone_certificate): Corollary 4.15, page 76, proved. For every fixed number J of strides, no strictly increasing function of x certifies descent over J Syracuse strides, because the odd integers congruent to minus 1 modulo 2 to the J+1 ascend for J strides in a row.
- [Main result: Noise bound for Switching MM uniform in the normalized step](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_variance_bound_uniform_in_normalized_step): Proposition 8.7, page 128, proved. On a quadratic with additive gradient noise, on every eigendirection with normalized step up to one, the stationary variance of Switching MM lies between that of gradient descent and 5/3 times it, uniformly over momentum coefficients below one, whereas every step momentum amplifies slow mode noise by a factor that grows without bound as the coefficient tends to one.
- [Main result: Gain weight theorem for the noise floor of periodic first order methods](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#gain_weight_theorem): Theorem 8.12, page 133, proved. For any linear periodic first order method on a quadratic that is stable at zero normalized step and has positive total gain, the slow mode noise floor at matched speed relative to gradient descent is a Cauchy and Schwarz ratio of the step gains, at least one, and equal to one only when all gains are equal.
- [Main result: Exact linear rate of Switching MM on smooth strongly convex functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_linear_rate_on_smooth_strongly_convex_functions): Theorem 9.9, page 169, proved. For strongly convex and L smooth functions, two steps of Switching MM at step one over L contract the distance to the minimizer by the product of the classical one step factors of a long and a short gradient step, which explicit functions show is the exact worst case over the class, and the function gap by its square, using the one step function value bound of Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur (2018).
- [Main result: Diophantine insufficiency, infinitely many cycle lengths survive any verification range](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#diophantine_insufficiency_cycle_lengths): Proposition 11.20, page 210, proved. However far the verification of the Collatz conjecture is pushed, infinitely many cycle lengths survive the cycle inequality, so information about the approximation of log2 3 alone cannot exclude all nontrivial cycles, a point Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (1997) made earlier in another form.
- [Main result: Residue certificates cannot prove descent for all integers (the exceptional 2 adic set)](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#residue_certificates_cannot_prove_descent_for_all_integers): Proposition 15.1, page 273, proved. No residue certificate of finite level can certify descent for every integer, because every residue class it leaves uncovered contains infinitely many positive integers, while the 2 adic integers with infinite coefficient stopping time form a closed null set that contains a point of each known negative cycle.
- [Main result: Sharp minimum inequality for cycles of the Syracuse map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#sharp_minimum_inequality): Theorem 18.3, page 309, proved. The smallest element of a cycle is below a bound that depends only on the number of odd elements and the closing defect, with constant 1/(2 log 2) in place of 1, uniformly in the word.
- [Main result: Christoffel cycles attain the sharp minimum inequality](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#christoffel_cycles_are_extremal): Theorem 18.5, page 310, proved. The positive rational cycle of the lower Christoffel word of slope s/r has 3 M_w Lambda between 2 to the minus 2 delta times beta_r = r/(2 log 2) + 1/4 + O(1/r) and the sharp bound B_r(delta), and along the rungs the ratio to the sharp bound tends to 1, so no inequality in r, s and the minimum alone can improve the constant 1/(2 log 2).
- [Open: Problem S5: Beyond the temperature law](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#beyond_the_temperature_law_problem): Problem S5, page 148
- [Open: Transient bound conjecture for the injection matrix of Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_transient_bound_conjecture): Conjecture 9.7, page 169
- [Conditional: Every switching rule between descent and injection is stable on quadratics, conditional on the transient bound](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#every_switching_rule_is_stable_on_quadratics): Corollary 9.8, page 169
- [Open: Exact convex worst case of Switching MM (conjecture)](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_exact_worst_case_conjecture): Conjecture 10.6, page 180
- [Conditional: What arithmetic would suffice to exclude all Collatz cycles](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#what_arithmetic_would_suffice): Corollary 11.22, page 213
- [Open: Cesàro liminf conjecture on the running mean of the halving exponents](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#cesaro_liminf_conjecture): Conjecture 12.6, page 230
- [Conditional: A bounded form of Tao's theorem would imply the Collatz conjecture, given the positive density theorems](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#bounded_tao_would_imply_collatz_given_positive_density): Proposition 13.3, page 247
- [Computed: Additive deficits of the second and third cumulants of total stopping times, fitted to the exact census](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#stopping_time_cumulant_deficits_census_fit): Proposition 17.1, page 296
- [Open: Conjectured exact worst case rate of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, both branches](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_exact_convex_rate_conjecture): Conjecture 17.2, page 298
- [Computed: Arithmetic gap at the rung r star: a rational cycle above 2 to the 71.41](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#arithmetic_gap_at_the_current_record_rung): Corollary 18.8, page 313
- [Open: Problem M1: records of the sharp ladder bound occur only at rungs](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#records_of_the_ladder_problem): Problem M1, page 321
- [Open: Problem M2: branch and bound exclusion of cycles at r = q_23](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#branch_and_bound_at_q23_problem): Problem M2, page 321
- [Open: Problem M3: an inequality for integer cycles that fails for some rational cycle](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#integer_cycle_inequality_problem): Problem M3, page 321
- [Open: Problem M4: counting admissible words with large Phi](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#words_with_large_phi_problem): Problem M4, page 322
- [Open: Problem M5: the limsup version of the finite modulus criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#limsup_version_problem): Problem M5, page 322
- [Open: Problem Q1: is seventeen states minimal for a beeping machine equivalent to the full Collatz conjecture](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#minimality_of_seventeen_states_problem): Problem Q1, page 333
- [Open: Problem Q2: a halting machine under the stopping time conjecture](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#halting_machine_under_the_stopping_time_conjecture_problem): Problem Q2, page 333

- [Open: Problem Q4: a deterministic density version of the excursion bound](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#deterministic_excursion_density_problem): Problem Q4, page 333
- [Open: Problem Q5: the state count at which the clock turns logarithmic](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#binary_encodings_problem): Problem Q5, page 333

- [Conditional: A polynomial tail bounds the least counterexample](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#polynomial_tail_bounds_the_least_counterexample): Corollary 20.21, page 352

## Computing the Riemann Hypothesis

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 1012 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, computed, conditional, open or counterexample), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 2.2.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Computing the Riemann Hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/index.html.md): by Nicholas G. Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Two volumes on the Thorin measure whose positivity is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, computed in certified ball arithmetic: Volume I on representations of Xi, Thorin measures and the reciprocal Xi function, Volume II on Cauchy deconvolution and certified computation. Keywords: Riemann hypothesis, zeros of the zeta function, Thorin measures, generalized gamma convolutions, Pólya densities, Brownian hitting times, reciprocal zeta function, de Bruijn Newman constant, Keiper Li coefficients, infinitely divisible distributions, Lee Yang theorem, certified ball arithmetic.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24086101): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24086101 for version 2.2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23331089 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html.md): 1012 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/main/RESULTS.md): 1012 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/releases/download/v2.2.0/computing_rh_vol1.pdf): 825 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/tree/v2.2.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Bosch type theorem for the reciprocal Xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_power_hcm_threshold): Volume I, Theorem 9.4.5, page 148, proved. The reciprocal Xi function composed with the power x to the p is HCM exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi, so RH is the extreme case p equal to one.
- [Main result: Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 1.16 x 10^25](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e25): Volume I, Theorem 8.1.14, page 118, proved. From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, every derivative of the heat trace alternates in sign, equivalently the Williamson measures are positive, up to order 1.16 times 10^25, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic.
- [Main result: Total variation distance from the Pólya law to ferromagnetic laws is below two millionths, with no hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_law_within_total_variation_two_millionths_of_a_ferromagnetic_law): Volume II, Proposition 18.1.17, page 555, proved. With no hypothesis the total variation distance from the Pólya law to the ferromagnetic laws is below 1.932 × 10^-6 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic and below 1.266 × 10^-4 by an explicit construction, below 6.024 × 10^-6 by a fitted law on a Bessel kernel (a note of Nicholas Polson), and it is zero exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
- [Main result: Phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#phase_diagram_theorem_de_bruijn_strip_theorem_in_thorin_form): Volume II, Theorem 5.3.2, page 96, proved. The set of points $(t,\alpha)$ where the shifted clock of the heat flow function is a generalized gamma convolution is carried along parabolas by the flow (de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form), the de Bruijn Newman constant is the minimum of $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2$ over it, and RH holds exactly when the corner $(0,\frac12)$ belongs to it.
- [Main result: All zeros of Xi are real if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a GGC, and real and simple if and only if it is the hitting time of a string](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_ggc_reciprocal_xi_law_and_to_the_existence_of_a_string): Volume I, Corollary 19.18.1, page 584, proved. RH holds if and only if $L$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with positive Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$; the zeros are all real and simple if and only if $L$ is the Laplace transform of the hitting time of a Krein string with positive mass; the same holds for any even real entire $\widehat H$ of order below two with $\widehat H(0)>0$.
- [Main result: The Thorin measure of reciprocal xi is absolutely continuous with the explicit density (1/pi) Re xi'/xi at every level from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#level_one_thorin_measure_explicit_density_with_prime_sum): Volume II, Theorem 9.1.1, page 180, proved. For every level $\theta\ge1$ the measure $\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ has real analytic density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$, at $\theta=1$ a gamma part minus a compensated prime sum, valid also at $v=0$.
- [Main result: Dichotomy for the band limited backward Cauchy flow from level one: convergence at level theta' if and only if zeta has no zeros to the right of theta'](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_cauchy_flow_converges_exactly_when_zeta_has_the_zero_free_half_plane): Volume II, Theorem 9.3.1, page 185, proved. The Fejér band limited backward flow from the level one measure converges to the level $\theta'$ Thorin measure if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, and has no measure limit if it has a zero there, so the Riemann hypothesis is convergence at every $\theta'>\frac12$.
- [Main result: Fifty three certified zeros on the critical line in a window at height 1e13 plus 100, above the verified range](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_zeros_on_the_critical_line_at_height_1e13_plus_100): Volume II, Result 11.8.7, page 289, computed. A ball arithmetic scan certifies 53 sign changes of Hardy's function, hence 53 zeros of zeta on the critical line, in a window centred at 1e13 plus 100, above the range verified by Platt and Trudgian; the count of zeros in the window and the real parts are not certified, and nothing is certified off the line.
- [Main result: Delta as the eighth power of the antipodal heat kernel of the sphere](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#delta_jacobi_antipodal_heat_kernel_on_sphere): Volume II, Theorem 23.4.1, page 705, proved. The cube of the Euler product equals the antipodal Brownian heat kernel on the 2 sphere times 4 pi and the law of a maximum of three exponential type maxima, so Delta is that kernel to the eighth power.
- [Main result: Ramanujan's lost notebook formula as a density with an RH criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#delta_ramanujan_lost_notebook_formula_as_density): Volume II, Theorem 23.7.1, page 714, proved. Ramanujan's transformation formula for the digamma sum is the density of an explicit random variable Z built from two Polya variables and an EGGC factor, and RH holds exactly when every zero of its characteristic function in the strip where the imaginary part has absolute value below one is real.
- [Main result: Beurling system with positive prime measure, polynomial growth and a zero off the critical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#beurling_system_with_zero_off_line_and_positive_primes): Volume II, Theorem 24.2.1, page 719, proved. An explicit Beurling system with a positive prime measure of density at most 2, a simple pole at 1, bounded growth in vertical strips and a power saving integer count has all its zeros at 0, rho and its conjugate, so the quasi Riemann hypothesis fails below beta for it.
- [Main result: Functional equation and positive integer measure force the Riemann zeta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#functional_equation_and_positive_integers_force_zeta): Volume II, Theorem 24.4.1, page 723, proved. A positive measure N on the integers of Beurling type whose Dirichlet series has the functional equation of zeta and finite order with only a pole at 1 is a multiple of the counting measure of the integers, so its zeta function is a multiple of zeta.
- [Main result: Level alpha dictionary, no zero right of alpha is equivalent to a GGC Thorin transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#iw_level_alpha_dictionary_qrh_ggc): Volume II, Theorem 22.3.1, page 670, proved. For an admissible L function and a level alpha at least one half, the shifted reciprocal Lambda(alpha)/Lambda(alpha+sqrt s) is a GGC transform if and only if there is no zero with real part above alpha, with an explicit Thorin density, extending the xi case to Dirichlet and elliptic curve L functions.
- [Main result: Positivity of the level alpha functional on nonnegative test functions is equivalent to QRH(alpha)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#iw_positivity_at_level_alpha_iff_qrh_alpha): Volume II, Proposition 22.5.3, page 675, proved. QRH(alpha) for zeta holds exactly when W_alpha is nonnegative on nonnegative band limited test functions, and already when it is nonnegative on an explicit two parameter family, which at alpha one half is the nontrivial direction of Weil's criterion.
- [Main result: What a zero free half plane gives the Thorin programme (conditional on no zero right of theta)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#qrh_conditional_thorin_programme_above_theta): Volume II, Corollary 21.3.1, page 647, conditional on zeta has no zero with real part above theta, for a given theta in [1/2,1). If zeta has no zero with real part above theta, then at every level above theta the shifted reciprocal of xi is a GGC transform with a positive Thorin density that has its strict minimum at the origin, the mass deficit vanishes, and the compensated prime sum converges at a stated rate; the converse also holds.
- [Open: Positivity of the Thorin density on one line, open question](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_line_positivity_exclusion_open): Volume I, Remark 2.1.5, page 23
- [Conditional: Residue expansion: absolute convergence of the density series given a lower bound for the derivative of xi at the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#absolutely_convergent_residue_series_for_the_density_given_a_lower_bound_for_xi_prime_at_zeros): Volume I, Theorem 5.3.2, page 56, conditional on the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros
- [Conditional: Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density near the origin, given the saddle point approximation](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#log_concavity_of_the_density_near_the_origin_given_the_saddle_point_approximation): Volume I, Proposition 5.7.3, page 62, conditional on the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives
- [Computed: Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density on [0.008, infinity) from computed constants](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_is_log_concave_from_0_008_given_computed_constants): Volume I, Theorem 5.7.5, page 64
- [Conditional: No HCM: sums of exponentials are not HCM, and the continued reciprocal xi density has a computed zero in the right half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_hcm_density_for_sums_of_exponentials_and_a_computed_zero_of_the_continued_density): Volume I, Theorem 5.7.7, page 66, conditional on for part (ii), an explicit remainder bound for the omitted terms on a sector containing $z_*$
- [Conditional: Prime built GGC hitting times converge to the base point laws for theta < beta < 2 - theta under QRH(theta)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#prime_built_ggc_hitting_times_converge_to_the_base_point_laws_under_qrh_theta): Volume I, Theorem 5.8.4, page 71, conditional on the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$) for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero has real part at most $\theta$)
- [Open: Question: is the Laplace transform E sech(sqrt(u) X) a GGC transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_arithmetic_mean_sech_is_ggc): Volume I, Problem 6.1, page 86
- [Open: Question: a class of mixing laws whose harmonic mean of GGC transforms is a GGC transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_harmonic_mean_class_of_mixing_laws): Volume I, Problem 6.2, page 86
- [Open: Question: a quantitative lower bound for Im M(-x - i eta)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_quantitative_bound_on_continuation_of_m): Volume I, Problem 6.3, page 86
- [Open: Question: even weights w for which w times Phi has a Fourier transform with only real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_even_weights_preserving_real_zeros_of_tilted_polya): Volume I, Problem 6.4, page 86
- [Conditional: A truncated EGGC law within v to the fourth times epsilon of the law of Y](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_zero_sum_is_eggc_close_to_y): Volume I, Proposition 7.7.2, page 96
- [Open: Question: is the BNKS mixing law the GGC of the z law proposition](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_mixing_law_of_bnks_z_laws): Volume I, Problem 7.1, page 97
- [Open: Question: positive sequences c_k for which the sum of L_k over c_k is a van Dantzig second member](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_sequences_giving_van_dantzig_pairs): Volume I, Problem 7.2, page 97
- [Open: Question: an unconditional EGGC family from the z law to Y other than the heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_family_of_eggc_laws_joining_z_law_to_y): Volume I, Problem 7.3, page 97
- [Open: Question: is the Lévy density K_t(y) of Y_t monotone in t](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_levy_density_of_y_t_monotone_in_t): Volume I, Problem 7.4, page 98
- [Open: Question: the set of lambda for which the ratio of transforms of T plus T tilde and H lambda is a Laplace transform](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_remainder_after_partial_h_infinity): Volume I, Problem 7.5, page 98
- [Conditional: There is no Gaussian smoothing criterion for RH on a line with real part alpha above one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_gaussian_criterion_on_vertical_line_alpha_above_one_half_under_rh): Volume I, Proposition 8.1.13, page 116, conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$

- [Counterexample: A harmonic mean of two GGC transforms that is not a Laplace transform of a positive measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#harmonic_mean_of_two_ggc_transforms_not_a_laplace_transform): Volume I, Example 11.1.24, page 219

## Elements of Bayes and Information Theory: A Predictive Theory of Inference: Information, Algorithms, and Large Deviations

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 60 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional, open or counterexample), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Elements of Bayes and Information Theory: A Predictive Theory of Inference: Information, Algorithms, and Large Deviations](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). A Bayesian statistics monograph built on de Finetti, Sanov and Bayes: exchangeable prediction under moment constraints gives maximum entropy laws, and testing, shrinkage, asymptotics and decision are read on one moderate deviation scale. Keywords: Bayesian statistics, information theory, de Finetti theorem, exchangeability, Sanov theorem, large deviations, moderate deviations, maximum entropy, Kullback Leibler divergence, e values, shrinkage priors, predictive inference.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24067804): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24067804 for version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24067803 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html.md): 60 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/elements_bayes_information/main/RESULTS.md): 60 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/elements_bayes_information/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/elements_bayes_information/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/elements_bayes_information/releases/download/v1.0.0/elements_bayes_information.pdf): 644 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/elements_bayes_information/tree/v1.0.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/elements_bayes_information/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Componentwise constrained horizon master inequality](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#constrained_horizon_master_inequality): Theorem 3.2, page 30, proved. A fixed block of coordinates drawn from a sample conditioned on a moment window is close in total variation to independent draws from the I projection, with an explicit finite sample bound with three separately controlled terms.
- [Main result: Projected de Finetti limit](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#projected_de_finetti_limit): Theorem 3.4, page 32, proved. After mixing over the constraint posterior, the block laws of an exchangeable sequence conditioned on a moment event converge to an exchangeable law whose random directing measure is the I projection of the original directing measure.
- [Main result: Decomposition of nonparametric predictive Bayes risk into Sanov and contraction terms](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#predictive_bayes_risk_decomposition): Theorem 4.1, page 59, proved. The predictive KL Bayes risk splits into a population Sanov term, a posterior contraction term and a small cross term, so misspecified models have risk equal to the Sanov term and well specified ones have risk equal to the contraction term.
- [Main result: Moderate scale calibration of tempered posteriors under misspecification](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#moderate_scale_calibration_misspecification): Proposition 7.31, page 272, proved. A scalar learning rate calibrates credible balls at moderate scale only when the model curvature and score covariance are proportional, and otherwise a matrix temperature is needed.
- [Main result: Generalized control variate estimator, optimal shrinkage and variance](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#generalized_control_variate_unification): Theorem 12.6, page 394, proved. The estimators of Bayes linear, cross prediction powered inference and inverse probability weighted prediction powered inference are all a baseline plus a shrunken labeled data rectifier, and the best shrinkage is a covariance over variance ratio.
- [Main result: Posterior contraction of the GBC maximum expected utility policy](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#gbc_meu_policy_posterior_contraction): Theorem 12.41, page 421, proved. Under a Lipschitz utility, posterior contraction at a rate and a quadratic margin condition, the policy that maximizes posterior expected utility converges in mean square to the oracle policy at a rate proportional to the contraction rate, so at rate N to the minus one quarter in parametric models.
- [Main result: Federated product of experts from exchangeability](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#federated_product_of_experts): Theorem 13.2, page 473, proved. If the pooled client data are exchangeable, the global posterior is the prior times the product of the client likelihoods, equivalently a product of size weighted local pseudo posteriors.
- [Conditional: Reachability and degeneracy of moment constraints](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#reachability_and_degeneracy): Proposition 3.7, page 34
- [Open: Optimal truncation at the moderate deviation scale](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#optimal_truncation_moderate_deviation_scale): Conjecture 4.15, page 72
- [Conditional: Adaptive Dirichlet process mixture predictive rate](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#adaptive_dpm_rate): Theorem 4.18, page 75, conditional on the data driven bandwidth stays within constant factors of the optimal bandwidth, which the book assumes and does not prove
- [Conditional: Adaptive Polya tree predictive rate](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#adaptive_polya_tree_rate): Theorem 4.19, page 76, conditional on the marginal likelihood truncation level stays within O(1) of the optimal level, which the book assumes and does not prove
- [Conditional: Adaptive logistic Gaussian process predictive rate](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#adaptive_logistic_gaussian_process_rate): Theorem 4.20, page 77
- [Conditional: Sharp log log n term in horseshoe super efficiency](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#horseshoe_super_efficiency_sharp_constant): Theorem 4.27, page 122
- [Open: Moderate deviation principle for non regular Ibragimov and Has'minskii models](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#mdp_principle_for_ih_models): Conjecture 4.41, page 138
- [Open: Modified asymptotic Bayes optimality under sparsity for the mild cusp](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#modified_abos_for_mild_cusp): Conjecture 4.43, page 139
- [Open: Weak ABOS for the horseshoe at the boundary beta one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#weak_abos_at_the_boundary): Conjecture 4.44, page 139
- [Open: Failure of asymptotic Bayes optimality for the strong cusp](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#abos_failure_for_strong_cusp): Conjecture 4.45, page 140
- [Open: ABOS of the beta horseshoe for exponential power noise](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#abos_of_the_beta_horseshoe): Conjecture 4.48, page 142
- [Conditional: Gaussian localization on the constraint chart](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#gaussian_localization_constraint_chart): Theorem 5.8, page 155
- [Conditional: Exchangeable block collapse under moment conditioning](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#exchangeable_block_collapse): Theorem 5.10, page 156
- [Conditional: Window robust collapse without lattice regularity](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#window_robust_collapse): Theorem 5.11, page 156
- [Conditional: Lifted collapse to the ambient predictive law under refinement](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#lifted_diagonal_collapse): Corollary 5.15, page 159
- [Conditional: Projection induced moment criterion is a generalized method of moments](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#projection_induced_moment_criterion): Proposition 5.20, page 163, conditional on the dual expansion proof in the Supplementary Material of the source paper, which the book does not reproduce
- [Counterexample: Mutual information Hessian in the channel parameter need not be positive semidefinite](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#mutual_information_hessian_not_psd): Proposition 5.33, page 188
- [Conditional: Calibration under dependent data and the long run variance](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#dependent_data_calibration): Proposition 7.34, page 275
- [Conditional: The Jeffreys prior equalizes the regret of the universal portfolio](https://vsokolov.org/books/elements_bayes_information/results.html#jeffreys_prior_equalizes_universal_portfolio_regret): Theorem 10.10, page 349, conditional on the Laplace expansion of the mixture wealth, which the book states without a formal proof

## Bayes, AI and Deep Learning: Foundations of Data Science

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 9 results has its exact statement, its status (conditional), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the Quarto file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.8 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayes, AI and Deep Learning: Foundations of Data Science](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). A textbook that develops Bayesian reasoning, statistical learning and deep learning as one probabilistic framework, from Bayes' rule and decision theory to neural networks, transformers and AI agents, with code in R and Python. Keywords: Bayesian learning, deep learning, statistical learning, large language models, neural networks, probabilistic inference, reinforcement learning, quantile neural networks, AI agents, transformer models, decision theory, Gaussian processes.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24060823): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24060823 for version 1.0.8 (10.5281/zenodo.23603836 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page

- [Main result: Posterior probability that Nakamura did not cheat given a 45 win streak](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#nakamura_streak_posterior_innocence): Example 2.10, page 77, conditional. Under Anand's prior of 1 in 10000 and a binomial model of the streak, the posterior probability that Nakamura did not cheat is 0.9965.
- [Main result: Polya Gamma Gibbs sampler for Bayesian logistic regression](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#polya_gamma_gibbs_sampler_logistic): Section 13.7.1, page 427, conditional. For binomial logistic regression with a Gaussian prior, alternating a Polya Gamma draw of one latent variable per observation with a multivariate normal draw of the coefficients gives a two step Gibbs sampler.
- [Main result: Posterior concentration at the minimax rate for sparse deep learning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#posterior_concentration_sparse_deep_learning): unnumbered, conditional. Under smoothness and prior mass conditions, the posterior distribution of the regression function concentrates around the true function at the minimax rate, up to a factor of log N.
- [Main result: Maximum expected utility by a quantile neural network](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#meu_quantile_network_method): Section 21.6.1, page 670, conditional. A network trained with the check loss on simulated utilities, with the decision and the quantile level as inputs, approximates the quantile function of the utility; integrating it over the level approximates the expected utility, and the optimal decision maximizes that integral.
- [Conditional: Posterior probability that Nakamura did not cheat given a 45 win streak](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#nakamura_streak_posterior_innocence): Example 2.10, page 77
- [Conditional: Option value of learning in Bernoulli Beta asset allocation](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#bernoulli_beta_option_value_of_learning): Section 4.2.3, page 156
- [Conditional: Livermore's trading maxims as Bellman value comparisons](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#livermore_maxims_bellman_view): Section 4.2.4, page 157
- [Conditional: Polya Gamma integral identity for binomial likelihoods](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#polya_gamma_integral_identity): Theorem 13.1, page 427
- [Conditional: Polya Gamma Gibbs sampler for Bayesian logistic regression](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#polya_gamma_gibbs_sampler_logistic): Section 13.7.1, page 427
- [Conditional: Bartlett Fejer scale mixture representation of the exponential power prior](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#bayesian_bridge_bartlett_fejer_mixture): Section 17.11.1, page 574
- [Conditional: Posterior concentration at the minimax rate for sparse deep learning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#posterior_concentration_sparse_deep_learning): unnumbered

## Bayesian Causality: Models, Accounting and the Bayesian Alternative to Double Machine Learning

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 20 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or conditional), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.2.1 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayesian Causality: Models, Accounting and the Bayesian Alternative to Double Machine Learning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). A textbook that builds one Bayesian model of outcomes given treatment and covariates and reads every causal quantity from its posterior, and compares it with double machine learning in simulations and in the 401(k), LaLonde and NHEFS data. Keywords: Bayesian causal inference, double machine learning, horseshoe prior, regularization induced confounding, heterogeneous treatment effects, posterior accounting identity, instrumental variables, difference in differences, sensitivity analysis and bounds, causal decisions.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23985916): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23985916 for version 1.2.1 (10.5281/zenodo.23899018 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html.md): 20 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/RESULTS.md): 20 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/releases/download/v1.2.1/bayesian_causality_book.pdf): 607 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/tree/v1.2.1): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Range of the average effect under a stable odds ratio](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#average_effect_range_under_case_mix): Proposition 4.3, page 55, proved. With one conditional odds ratio e^psi for every unit, the average risk difference over all possible case mixes fills the interval from 0 to tanh(psi/4), so the same stable effect supports very different averages.
- [Main result: The posterior selects the group](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#posterior_selects_the_group): Theorem 4.19, page 65, proved. The log posterior odds of one effect scale against another, or against the saturated model, move linearly in n at a rate equal to the difference of their information gaps, with a log n term for the difference in the number of parameters.
- [Main result: Exact error decomposition of the partialling out estimator](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#exact_error_decomposition_of_the_robinson_estimator): Lemma 5.3, page 83, proved. The error of the partialling out estimator splits exactly, with no approximation, into a noise term, a cross term with mean zero under cross fitting and a bias term built from the two fitting errors, namely their product minus the effect times the squared treatment error.
- [Main result: Two channels](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#two_channels_of_the_dml_bias): Corollary 5.4, page 84, proved. With the fits held fixed the estimator converges to the truth plus a bias fixed by the inner product of the two fitting errors and the squared treatment error.
- [Main result: No uniformly valid interval of finite length](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#no_uniformly_valid_interval_of_finite_length): Proposition 7.8, page 127, proved. For a fixed sample size, no confidence set for the partialling out effect can both have uniform coverage over all treatment variances and have expected length bounded over that class; the proof follows Gleser and Hwang (1987) and Dufour (1997).
- [Main result: Identification of the merger effect](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#merger_effect_depends_only_on_demand_and_conduct): Proposition 20.5, page 345, proved. Given the premerger data, the price effect of a merger is a function of the nonlinear demand parameters and the form of competition alone, so the agency question is a question about their posterior.
- [Conditional: Attenuation representation](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_causality_book/results.html#attenuation_representation): Theorem 7.5, page 121
- [Chapter 1. Causal Questions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/summaries/01_causal_questions.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 2. Frameworks for Causal Inference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/summaries/02_frameworks_for_causal_inference.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 3. Models, Accounting and Randomization](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/summaries/03_models_accounting_and_randomization.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 4. Groups, Urns and Information](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/summaries/04_groups_urns_and_information.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 5. What Double Machine Learning Assumes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/summaries/05_what_double_machine_learning_assumes.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 6. The Inverse Weighting Lineage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_causality_book/main/summaries/06_the_inverse_weighting_lineage.md): summary of the chapter and its results

## Clinical Trials in Practice: From Foundations to AI Agents

- [Clinical Trials in Practice: From Foundations to AI Agents](https://vsokolov.org/books/clinical_trials_in_practice/index.html.md): by Alexandra Sokolova and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Clinical trials as science and as regulated operations: design and statistics, the daily work of a Phase III study from site selection to the trial master file, regulatory submission, and what AI agents may and may not do in regulated research. Keywords: clinical trials, Phase III trials, clinical trial operations, adaptive trial design, Bayesian clinical trials, Good Clinical Practice, regulatory submission, trial master file, clinical data management, drug development, real world evidence, AI agents in clinical research.

## On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 208 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.4.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). What probability can and cannot contribute to the Langlands programme: Sato Tate laws, random walks on trees and isogeny graphs, Thorin measures and generalized gamma convolutions as reformulations of the Riemann hypothesis, and Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups, with code and data. Keywords: Langlands programme, Sato Tate law, Frobenius traces, automorphic L functions, generalized Riemann hypothesis, Thorin measures, generalized gamma convolutions, random walks on trees, supersingular isogeny graphs, random matrix theory, Poisson Dirichlet law, critical percolation, Bayesian inference.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23904867): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23904867 for version 1.4.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23419247 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html.md): 208 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/main/RESULTS.md): 208 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/releases/download/v1.4.0/langlands.pdf): 730 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/tree/v1.4.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Equidistribution does not determine automorphy](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#equidistribution_does_not_determine_automorphy): Proposition 1.5, page 7, proved. Sato Tate equidistribution of a sequence indexed by the primes cannot certify that it comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) with trivial central character, because altering such a sequence on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves the limiting empirical averages of all continuous functions unchanged but, by Ramakrishnan's refinement of strong multiplicity one, makes it nonautomorphic, and continuum many equidistributed sequences are not automorphic.
- [Main result: Limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kemeny_constant_supersingular_isogeny_graphs_limit): Theorem 11.6, page 166, proved. As the characteristic grows through primes congruent to 1 modulo 12, with the prime isogeny degree fixed, the mean time for simple random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph to hit a uniformly random curve is asymptotic to the number of vertices times the expected number of visits of simple random walk on the regular tree of the same degree to its starting point, so about twice the number of vertices for 2 isogenies.
- [Main result: Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of automorphic L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_criteria_generalized_riemann_hypothesis_automorphic): Theorem 15.8, page 235, proved. The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the L function of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, and the Riemann hypothesis for zeta, are each equivalent to several positivity statements, among them that the reciprocal of the self dual completion, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure sits at the squared ordinates of the zeros, and a Hankel criterion computable from central derivatives; the theorem is an equivalence that extends the first author's 2018 paper, and it proves no case of either hypothesis.
- [Main result: Thorin criterion for the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at a prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#ramanujan_petersson_local_thorin_criterion): Corollary 16.4, page 253, proved. For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over the rationals with trivial central character, the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at an unramified prime (outside the degenerate case of trace 2) holds exactly when the reciprocal of the symmetrised Euler factor, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, which is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb (Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin); the corollary is an equivalence and proves no case of the conjecture.
- [Main result: Thorin structure of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_structure_hecke_walk_passage_times_tree): Theorem 16.15, page 261, proved. The first time that continuous time simple random walk on a regular tree (the Hecke walk, on the Bruhat Tits tree when the degree is a prime plus one) reaches distance n from its start is a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin atoms, given by the zeros of the sphere polynomials of the tree, lie in the Kesten band and follow the arcsine law as n grows, with an exact mean, a variance linear in n and a central limit theorem; Thorin support in the Kesten band is the random walk form of the Ramanujan bound, and this unconditional theorem about the tree proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms.
- [Main result: Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#frobenius_labelled_factorisation_gamma_process_limit): Theorem 21.18, page 365, proved. As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, the logarithms of its prime power factors, multiplied by the parameter minus one and labelled by any equidistributed sequence of points such as Frobenius classes or Sato Tate angles, converge in law to the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator carrying independent labels drawn from the equidistribution law, and the labelled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma random measure, so that equidistribution becomes a Gamma process.
- [Main result: Extreme value representation of L functions of eta products](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#extreme_value_representation_of_eta_product_l_functions): Theorem 31.7, page 568, proved. For every eta product, that is every product of the functions eta(m tau) raised to nonnegative integer powers r_m with the sum of m r_m equal to 24 (the thirty multiplicative eta products among them), the L function is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at an explicit maximum of exponential clocks, so its values at positive real points are probabilities strictly between zero and one that increase strictly to one.
- [Main result: Consistency of Bayes factors under equidistribution](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#consistency_of_bayes_factors_under_equidistribution): Theorem 33.1, page 598, proved. For any deterministic sequence, such as normalised Frobenius traces, that is equidistributed for a true law with finitely many atoms and finite Kullback Leibler divergence from one candidate law, and with a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor between two candidate laws is asymptotically linear in the number of observations, and as the clipping level grows its slope tends to the difference of the divergences of the true law from the two candidates, with no independence assumed.
- [Open: Sato Tate discrepancy vanishes at the square root scale in logarithmic density](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_discrepancy_logarithmic_density_conjecture): Conjecture 5.3, page 68
